# E0400: `inout` argument marked wrongly

An argument for an `inout` parameter is marked `inout` at the call, as `bump(inout count)`, so that a change to it is visible there; no other argument is.

- Rule: [`expressions.inout-arguments`](../../reference/08-expressions.md#expressions.inout-arguments)
- Reported at: the argument.
- Tier: `core`, checked in the `types` phase

## Example

This program makes the mistake:

```stilt E0400:5
fn bump(inout count: i64) { count += 1 }

fn twice(inout count: i64) {
  bump(inout count)
  bump(count)
}
```

This one is fixed:

```stilt
fn bump(inout count: i64) { count += 1 }

fn twice(inout count: i64) {
  bump(inout count)
  bump(inout count)
}
```

## What the compiler prints

`stilt check` on [`E0400_inout_argument_marked_wrongly.lt`](../../tests/diagnostics/E0400_inout_argument_marked_wrongly.lt):

```text
── `inout` ARGUMENT MARKED WRONGLY ── E0400_inout_argument_marked_wrongly.lt:5:8  [E0400]

This parameter is `inout`, so its argument is marked `inout`:

  5 │   bump(count)
    │        ^^^^^

An argument for an `inout` parameter is marked `inout` at the call, as
`bump(inout count)`, so that a change to it is visible there; no other argument
is.

To fix it, mark it `inout`:

  5 │   bump(inout count)
    │        ++++++
```
